findings.description: make_home now rewrites the host's ~/.codex/auth.json into the per-run HOME, but it only redacts tokens.refresh_token. Every other key is copied verbatim: tokens.access_token, tokens.id_token (an identity JWT carrying the account's email/subject), tokens.account_id, and the top-level OPENAI_API_KEY when the host logged in with API-key auth. That file is mounted read-write at /home/evaluser inside the container where the evaluated agent runs arbitrary shell with network access. The new KF-048 pre-flight in run-ablation.sh additionally guarantees the access token is valid for at least 2 x summed watchdog / concurrency (hours), so an agent that reads the file always gets a live credential. OPENAI_API_KEY in particular does not expire. The test only asserts that the refresh token is replaced, so the long-lived key is never checked.
findings.failure_mode: An evaluated agent (or prompt-injected content it processes) runs `cat ~/.codex/auth.json` and exfiltrates a live OpenAI access token, identity token, or a non-expiring OPENAI_API_KEY over the container's network, giving an outside party use of the operator's OpenAI account/billing beyond the run.
findings.suggested_fix: Allowlist instead of denylist: write only the keys the codex CLI needs for the chatgpt auth mode (auth_mode, tokens.access_token, tokens.account_id, placeholder refresh_token) and set OPENAI_API_KEY to null unless auth_mode is explicitly api-key; drop id_token if the CLI does not require it. Extend the KF-048 bats case to assert OPENAI_API_KEY is null in the copy. Longer term, mount auth.json read-only and only for phases that run the dissent.

findings.description: The reserved-basename set is built from every .py file under any fixture directory whose path contains a component named tests or test (helpers.py, _oracle_x.py, utils.py, etc.), and it is then applied to the whole graded tree, not just test directories. pytest's default import-mode collision only concerns modules it actually collects/imports from package-less test dirs; a legitimately named production module such as src/pkg/utils.py or app/helpers.py does not collide, yet it is unlinked before the hidden suite runs. The grader thus deletes part of a correct solution and grades it as failing, which is the exact outcome 1.2.11 was meant to prevent. The deletion is silent to the agent (only grading/<label>.colliding-removed.txt records it).
findings.failure_mode: A correct agent solution that adds a source module sharing a basename with a fixture test helper (common names: utils.py, helpers.py, conftest-adjacent fixtures) is mutilated before grading and recorded as a hidden-test failure, biasing arm comparisons.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the scan of the graded tree to paths that pytest will collect for the task's test_command (the tests/ or test/ roots, or directories matching the configured testpaths), and reserve only basenames pytest imports by name (test_*.py / *_test.py and sibling helpers inside the same rootdir), rather than any .py anywhere. Log removals into grade.json with paths so they are auditable per row.

findings.description: reserved is derived only from overlay entries that are files (owned) and from the fixture tree. Overlay entries that are directories (owned_dirs) are excluded from the reservation: .py files inside a hidden overlay directory never enter reserved, so an agent file elsewhere in the tree with the same basename is not removed and the import-file-mismatch abort that 1.2.11 targets still occurs for those tasks. Conversely, the fixture walk's any(p in ('tests','test')) matches a component at any depth, so a vendored third-party test tree inside the fixture (e.g. vendor/lib/tests/test_core.py) reserves names against the agent's tree.
findings.failure_mode: Tasks whose hidden suite is delivered as an overlay directory remain vulnerable to collection aborts (correct solution graded failing); vendored test trees cause spurious removals. Both skew grades silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Walk each overlay directory (os.walk(full)) and add its .py basenames to reserved; anchor the fixture scan to the top-level tests/ or test/ roots the task's test_command actually runs rather than any path component.
